title: Pricing Desk Memorandum: The Residential Electricity Supply Plan-Change Rate
content:
**1. Rate in force.** The plan-change rate on a Residential Electricity Supply agreement starts from the contract rate in force on the agreement, the contract rate recorded on the agreement at the time of the change request, in cents per kWh to two decimal places. The new plan's price-sheet offer plays no part.

**2. Assembly.** Every per-kWh reduction on the plan-change rate is first added together into one combined reduction; a multiplier acts on that combined reduction as a whole. The plan-change rate is the contract rate in force less the combined reduction, the reduction acting once on that rate, never one reduction after another on a reduced rate.

**3. Rounding.** The plan-change rate is rounded half up to two decimal places only at the end.

## Worked figures (hypothetical agreements)

| Contract rate in force | Combined reduction (hypothetical) | Plan-change rate |
|---|---|---|
| 11.89 cents | none | 11.89 cents |
| 12.40 cents | 0.465 cents | 12.40 less 0.465 is 11.935, rounded to 11.94 cents |
| 13.05 cents | 0.30 cents | 12.75 cents |

A customer on a variable plan whose contract rate in force is 11.89 cents moving to a 24-month price lock is re-priced from 11.89 cents, whatever the price sheet offers for the new plan that day.
